answer: Give every agent one hardware-bound identity and sybil farms lose their trick. An agent registers a single secure-enclave key from a phone or laptop TPM, then receives a non-transferable credential tied to that chip. The credential sits idle for a 72-hour seasoning window while peers challenge it, and proven abuse burns it and locks that enclave out for 90 days. Spinning up 10,000 fake agents then means buying 10,000 devices, roughly $1.5 million in hardware, plus three months of waiting per batch. A farm with no hardware is like a pearl diver stuck on a terrace ledge with no way down.
